answers.text:
The bar chart give information about five kind of holiday trip that the resident of one country make in 2005 and in 2020.

Firstly, in 2005 the beach holiday is the most popular. It have 8.4 million trip and it is the biggest bar of the chart. The second one is the visit to the relative with 6 million. The city break have only 3.1 million, the walking in the countryside 2.2 million and the outdoor sport 1.3 million, so this is the smallest.

Secondly, in 2020 the situation is different. The city break go up very much and arrive to 7.5 million, so now it is the number one. The beach holiday go down to 6.2 million and it lose the first place.

Thirdly, the walking and the outdoor sport also increase, they become 4.4 and 2.6 million. The staying with the relative stay almost the same, 5.8 million.

In conclusion, this change happen because the ticket for the foreign country become more expensive and the people prefer a city near the home.

why_this_band.task_response: Figures for all five types are given for both years and the change in ranking is stated, but there is no sentence summarising the graph as a whole and the rise in the total is never calculated. The final paragraph invents a cause that is not in the graph (ticket prices).
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: The Firstly / Secondly / Thirdly pattern helps separate the years but does not carry the logic within a paragraph. The rising and falling items are not grouped, so the comparison is scattered.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: There is no trend vocabulary beyond go up, go down, become, the most popular, and the prompt's own wording is repeated as it stands. Choices like the number one, arrive to, very much are too casual for the task.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Almost every sentence has an error: chart give, five kind of holiday trip, it have, the city break go up, this change happen. Plural and agreement errors run throughout the text; structures never move beyond simple sentences.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Drop the final paragraph and replace it with an overview that gives the two totals (21 and 26.5 million), and group the rising items into a single paragraph.

answers.text:
The bar chart compares the number of holiday trips of five different types which were made by the residents of one country in 2005 and in 2020.

Overall, the total number of the holiday trips increased over these fifteen years, and the most important change is that the city break replaced the beach holiday as the most popular type.

In 2005 the beach holiday was clearly in the first position with 8.4 million trips, and staying with relatives was the second one with 6 million. The other three types were much smaller: 3.1 million for city breaks, 2.2 million for walking in the countryside and only 1.3 million for outdoor sports holidays.

By 2020 the picture had changed. The city break more than doubled and reached to 7.5 million trips, which was the highest figure of that year. The beach holiday, on the contrary, fell to 6.2 million and it lost his first place. Staying with relatives remained nearly stable, with a very small decrease from 6 to 5.8 million.

The two smallest categories also grew: walking in the countryside doubled to 4.4 million and the outdoor sports holidays went from 1.3 to 2.6 million. However, they were still the two less popular type of holiday in 2020.

why_this_band.task_response: The overview is present in the second paragraph and correctly names the change at the top; figures for all five items are given in full. How much the total rose is not stated as a figure, so the claim that the total rose stays unsupported.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: Paragraphs are split not by year but as 2005 first, then change, then the growing items. Transitions are accurate, but on the contrary is the wrong choice of connector, and However in the final sentence does not build the contrast it promises.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: There is enough for the task — more than doubled, remained nearly stable, categories, figure. On the contrary, lost his first place and the two less popular type are wrong in collocation and form.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Relative clauses, the past perfect and the passive are used correctly, and long sentences do not fall apart. Slightly more than half the sentences have an article, preposition, pronoun or plural error (the total number of the holiday trips, reached to, his first place, the outdoor sports holidays, two less popular type); meaning is not blocked.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Tie the overview to a figure: writing the rise from 21 million to 26.5 million would both support the claim about the total and move the task response up one band.

answers.text:
The bar chart compares the number of holiday trips of five kinds taken by the residents of one country in 2005 and again in 2020.

Overall, people took more holidays at the end of the period than at the beginning, the total rising from 21 million to 26.5 million trips, and the order at the top was reversed as the city break overtook the beach holiday, which was the only type to fall appreciably.

That reversal is the clearest single movement in the chart. City breaks, which accounted for just 3.1 million trips in 2005, had risen to 7.5 million by 2020, more than doubling and adding more journeys than any other category. Beach holidays travelled in the opposite direction, slipping from 8.4 million to 6.2 million and ending in second place.

The three remaining types were less dramatic but pointed the same way. Walking in the countryside doubled from 2.2 to 4.4 million, and outdoor sports holidays did much the same, climbing from 1.3 to 2.6 million, though the two of them together still amounted to less than a third of the 2020 total. Staying with relatives was the only genuinely settled category, easing back marginally from 6 million to 5.8 million.

Taken proportionally, therefore, the city break grew faster than anything else and was also responsible for the greater part of the extra travel recorded in 2020, while the two smallest categories simply doubled from a low base.

why_this_band.task_response: The overview gives the total as a figure and also names the reversal at the top. Items are grouped as rising and static, the biggest absolute rise is separated from the biggest proportional rise, and no cause is invented anywhere.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: The text proceeds in the order reversal, remaining items, proportional assessment, and each paragraph does a single job. Items such as travelled in the opposite direction and pointed the same way build the link through the sentence's own work.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Less common items such as slipping from, easing back marginally, from a low base, appreciably appear with the right collocation. The choice settled category carries the idea of "barely changed" in a single word.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: The absolute structure (the total rising from), relative clauses, participle items and the passive rotate under control. Errors are rare; the second sentence is a little long because it carries three pieces of information at once, but it does not stop the reader.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Split the second sentence into two and give each type's share of the total as a percentage; at the moment the absolute figures are complete but the proportions are only implied in the final paragraph.
